title: Pizza crust
summary: A thin, crisp-bottomed pizza base from almond flour and psyllium, pre-baked so it holds any topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) with a baking sheet or pizza stone inside.
Whisk the almond flour, psyllium, baking powder and salt. Add the egg, olive oil, warm water and garlic and mix to a firm dough. Rest 10 minutes.
Roll between two sheets of parchment into a 30 cm (12 in) round, about 5 mm (¼ in) thick. Remove the top sheet and prick all over with a fork.
Slide the crust on its parchment onto the hot sheet or stone and bake 10–12 minutes, until set and lightly golden.
Add toppings and bake 6–8 minutes more, until hot and browned at the edge.
tips: Keep toppings light and not too wet; a grain-free crust softens under a heavy, watery sauce.
Carbs shown are for the crust only — add your toppings' carbs.

origin.history: Flatbreads with toppings are ancient around the Mediterranean, but pizza as we know it took shape in Naples in the 1700s and 1800s, sold as cheap street food. A popular story says the Margherita was named for Queen Margherita's visit in 1889, though the details are disputed. Italian emigrants carried pizza worldwide in the twentieth century.
